2202 """
2203 abstract type AbstractBVPFunction{iip, twopoint} <: AbstractDiffEqFunction{iip} end
2204
2205 @doc doc"""
2206 $(TYPEDEF)
2207
2208 A representation of a BVP function `f`, defined by:
2209
2210 ```math
2211 \frac{du}{dt} = f(u, p, t)
2212 ```
2213
2214 and the constraints:
2215
2216 ```math
2217 g(u, p, t) = 0
2218 ```
2219
2220 If the size of `g(u, p, t)` is different from the size of `u`, then the constraints are
2221 interpreted as a least squares problem, i.e. the objective function is:
2222
2223 ```math
2224 \min_{u} \| g_i(u, p, t) \|^2
2225 ```
2226
2227 and all of its related functions, such as the Jacobian of `f`, its gradient
2228 with respect to time, and more. For all cases, `u0` is the initial condition,
2229 `p` are the parameters, and `t` is the independent variable.
2230
2231 ```julia
2232 BVPFunction{iip, specialize}(f, bc;
2233 cost = __has_cost(f) ? f.cost : nothing,
2234 equality = __has_equality(f) ? f.equality : nothing,
2235 inequality = __has_inequality(f) ? f.inequality : nothing,
2236 f_prototype = __has_f_prototype(f) ? f.f_prototype : nothing,
2237 mass_matrix = __has_mass_matrix(f) ? f.mass_matrix : I,
2238 analytic = __has_analytic(f) ? f.analytic : nothing,
2239 tgrad= __has_tgrad(f) ? f.tgrad : nothing,
2240 jac = __has_jac(f) ? f.jac : nothing,
2241 bcjac = __has_jac(bc) ? bc.jac : nothing,
2242 jvp = __has_jvp(f) ? f.jvp : nothing,
2243 vjp = __has_vjp(f) ? f.vjp : nothing,
2244 jac_prototype = __has_jac_prototype(f) ? f.jac_prototype : nothing,
2245 bcjac_prototype = __has_jac_prototype(bc) ? bc.jac_prototype : nothing,
2246 sparsity = __has_sparsity(f) ? f.sparsity : jac_prototype,
2247 paramjac = __has_paramjac(f) ? f.paramjac : nothing,
2248 syms = nothing,
2249 indepsym= nothing,
2250 paramsyms = nothing,
2251 colorvec = __has_colorvec(f) ? f.colorvec : nothing,
2252 bccolorvec = __has_colorvec(f) ? bc.colorvec : nothing,
2253 sys = __has_sys(f) ? f.sys : nothing,
2254 twopoint::Union{Val, Bool} = Val(false))
2255 ```
2256
2257 Note that both the function `f` and boundary condition `bc` are required. `f` should
2258 be given as `f(du,u,p,t)` or `out = f(u,p,t)`. `bc` should be given as `bc(res, u, p, t)`.
2259 See the section on `iip` for more details on in-place vs out-of-place handling.
2260
2261 All of the remaining functions are optional for improving or accelerating
2262 the usage of `f` and `bc`. These include:
2263
2264 - `cost(u, p)`: the target to be minimized, similar with the `cost` function
2265 in `OptimizationFunction`. This is used to define the objective function
2266 of the BVP, which can be minimized by optimization solvers.
2267 - `equality(res, u, t)`: equality constraints functions for the BVP.
2268 - `inequality(res, u, t)`: inequality constraints functions for the BVP.
2269 - `f_prototype`: a prototype matrix matching the type of the ODE/DAE variables in an optimal control
2270 problem. For example, in the ODE/DAE that describe the dynamics of the optiml control problem,
2271 `f_prototype` should match the type and size of the ODE/DAE variables in `f`.
2272 - `mass_matrix`: the mass matrix `M` represented in the BVP function. Can be used
2273 to determine that the equation is actually a BVP for differential algebraic equation (DAE)
2274 if `M` is singular.
2275 - `analytic(u0,p,t)`: used to pass an analytical solution function for the analytical
2276 solution of the BVP. Generally only used for testing and development of the solvers.
2277 - `tgrad(dT,u,h,p,t)` or dT=tgrad(u,p,t): returns ``\frac{\partial f(u,p,t)}{\partial t}``
2278 - `jac(J,du,u,p,gamma,t)` or `J=jac(du,u,p,gamma,t)`: returns ``\frac{df}{du}``
2279 - `bcjac(J,du,u,p,gamma,t)` or `J=jac(du,u,p,gamma,t)`: returns ``\frac{dbc}{du}``
2280 - `jvp(Jv,v,du,u,p,gamma,t)` or `Jv=jvp(v,du,u,p,gamma,t)`: returns the directional
2281 derivative ``\frac{df}{du} v``
2282 - `vjp(Jv,v,du,u,p,gamma,t)` or `Jv=vjp(v,du,u,p,gamma,t)`: returns the adjoint
2283 derivative ``\frac{df}{du}^\ast v``
2284 - `jac_prototype`: a prototype matrix matching the type that matches the Jacobian. For example,
2285 if the Jacobian is tridiagonal, then an appropriately sized `Tridiagonal` matrix can be used
2286 as the prototype and integrators will specialize on this structure where possible. Non-structured
2287 sparsity patterns should use a `SparseMatrixCSC` with a correct sparsity pattern for the Jacobian.
2288 The default is `nothing`, which means a dense Jacobian.
2289 - `bcjac_prototype`: a prototype matrix matching the type that matches the Jacobian. For example,
2290 if the Jacobian is tridiagonal, then an appropriately sized `Tridiagonal` matrix can be used
2291 as the prototype and integrators will specialize on this structure where possible. Non-structured
2292 sparsity patterns should use a `SparseMatrixCSC` with a correct sparsity pattern for the Jacobian.
2293 The default is `nothing`, which means a dense Jacobian.
2294 - `paramjac(pJ,u,p,t)`: returns the parameter Jacobian ``\frac{df}{dp}``.
2295 - `colorvec`: a color vector according to the SparseDiffTools.jl definition for the sparsity
2296 pattern of the `jac_prototype`. This specializes the Jacobian construction when using
2297 finite differences and automatic differentiation to be computed in an accelerated manner
2298 based on the sparsity pattern. Defaults to `nothing`, which means a color vector will be
2299 internally computed on demand when required. The cost of this operation is highly dependent
2300 on the sparsity pattern.
2301 - `bccolorvec`: a color vector according to the SparseDiffTools.jl definition for the sparsity
2302 pattern of the `bcjac_prototype`. This specializes the Jacobian construction when using
2303 finite differences and automatic differentiation to be computed in an accelerated manner
2304 based on the sparsity pattern. Defaults to `nothing`, which means a color vector will be
2305 internally computed on demand when required. The cost of this operation is highly dependent
2306 on the sparsity pattern.
2307
2308 Additional Options:
2309
2310 - `twopoint`: Specify that the BVP is a two-point boundary value problem. Use `Val(true)` or
2311 `Val(false)` for type stability.
2312
2313 ## iip: In-Place vs Out-Of-Place
2314
2315 For more details on this argument, see the ODEFunction documentation.
2316
2317 ## specialize: Controlling Compilation and Specialization
2318
2319 For more details on this argument, see the ODEFunction documentation.
2320
2321 ## Fields
2322
2323 The fields of the BVPFunction type directly match the names of the inputs.
2324 """
2325 struct BVPFunction{
2326 iip, specialize, twopoint, F, BF, C, EC, IC, FP, TMM, Ta, Tt, TJ, BCTJ, JVP, VJP,
2327 JP, BCJP, BCRP, SP, TW, TWt, TPJ, O, TCV, BCTCV,
2328 SYS, ID} <: AbstractBVPFunction{iip, twopoint}
2329 f::F
2330 bc::BF
2331 cost::C
2332 equality::EC
2333 inequality::IC
2334 f_prototype::FP
2335 mass_matrix::TMM
2336 analytic::Ta
2337 tgrad::Tt
2338 jac::TJ
2339 bcjac::BCTJ
2340 jvp::JVP
2341 vjp::VJP
2342 jac_prototype::JP
2343 bcjac_prototype::BCJP
2344 bcresid_prototype::BCRP
2345 sparsity::SP
2346 Wfact::TW
2347 Wfact_t::TWt
2348 paramjac::TPJ
2349 observed::O
2350 colorvec::TCV
2351 bccolorvec::BCTCV
2352 sys::SYS
2353 initialization_data::ID
2354 end

2356 @doc doc"""
2357 $(TYPEDEF)
2358
2359 A representation of a dynamical BVP function `f`, defined by:
2360
2361 ```math
2362 M \frac{ddu}{dt} = f(du,u,p,t)
2363 ```
2364
2365 along with its boundary condition:
2366
2367 ```math
2368
2369 ```
2370
2371 and all of its related functions, such as the Jacobian of `f`, its gradient
2372 with respect to time, and more. For all cases, `u0` is the initial condition,
2373 `p` are the parameters, and `t` is the independent variable.
2374
2375 ## Constructor
2376
2377 ```julia
2378 DynamicalBVPFunction{iip,specialize}(f, bc;
2379 mass_matrix = __has_mass_matrix(f) ? f.mass_matrix : I,
2380 analytic = __has_analytic(f) ? f.analytic : nothing,
2381 tgrad= __has_tgrad(f) ? f.tgrad : nothing,
2382 jac = __has_jac(f) ? f.jac : nothing,
2383 jvp = __has_jvp(f) ? f.jvp : nothing,
2384 vjp = __has_vjp(f) ? f.vjp : nothing,
2385 jac_prototype = __has_jac_prototype(f) ? f.jac_prototype : nothing,
2386 sparsity = __has_sparsity(f) ? f.sparsity : jac_prototype,
2387 paramjac = __has_paramjac(f) ? f.paramjac : nothing,
2388 colorvec = __has_colorvec(f) ? f.colorvec : nothing,
2389 sys = __has_sys(f) ? f.sys : nothing
2390 twopoint::Union{Val, Bool} = Val(false))
2391 ```
2392
2393 Note that only the functions `f_i` themselves are required. These functions should
2394 be given as `f_i!(du,du,u,p,t)` or `ddu = f_i(du,u,p,t)`. See the section on `iip`
2395 for more details on in-place vs out-of-place handling.
2396
2397 All of the remaining functions are optional for improving or accelerating
2398 the usage of `f`. These include:
2399
2400 - `mass_matrix`: the mass matrix `M_i` represented in the ODE function. Can be used
2401 to determine that the equation is actually a differential-algebraic equation (DAE)
2402 if `M` is singular. Note that in this case special solvers are required, see the
2403 DAE solver page for more details: https://docs.sciml.ai/DiffEqDocs/stable/solvers/dae_solve/.
2404 Must be an AbstractArray or an AbstractSciMLOperator. Should be given as a tuple
2405 of mass matrices, i.e. `(M_1, M_2)` for the mass matrices of equations 1 and 2
2406 respectively.
2407 - `analytic(u0,p,t)`: used to pass an analytical solution function for the analytical
2408 solution of the ODE. Generally only used for testing and development of the solvers.
2409 - `tgrad(dT,du,u,p,t)` or dT=tgrad(du,u,p,t): returns ``\frac{\partial f(du,u,p,t)}{\partial t}``
2410 - `jac(J,du,u,p,t)` or `J=jac(du,u,p,t)`: returns ``\frac{df}{du}``
2411 - `jvp(Jv,v,u,p,t)` or `Jv=jvp(v,u,p,t)`: returns the directional derivative ``\frac{df}{du} v``
2412 - `vjp(Jv,v,u,p,t)` or `Jv=vjp(v,u,p,t)`: returns the adjoint derivative ``\frac{df}{du}^\ast v``
2413 - `jac_prototype`: a prototype matrix matching the type that matches the Jacobian. For example,
2414 if the Jacobian is tridiagonal, then an appropriately sized `Tridiagonal` matrix can be used
2415 as the prototype and integrators will specialize on this structure where possible. Non-structured
2416 sparsity patterns should use a `SparseMatrixCSC` with a correct sparsity pattern for the Jacobian.
2417 The default is `nothing`, which means a dense Jacobian.
2418 - `paramjac(pJ,du,u,p,t)`: returns the parameter Jacobian ``\frac{df}{dp}``.
2419 - `colorvec`: a color vector according to the SparseDiffTools.jl definition for the sparsity
2420 pattern of the `jac_prototype`. This specializes the Jacobian construction when using
2421 finite differences and automatic differentiation to be computed in an accelerated manner
2422 based on the sparsity pattern. Defaults to `nothing`, which means a color vector will be
2423 internally computed on demand when required. The cost of this operation is highly dependent
2424 on the sparsity pattern.
2425
2426 ## iip: In-Place vs Out-Of-Place
2427
2428 For more details on this argument, see the ODEFunction documentation.
2429
2430 ## specialize: Controlling Compilation and Specialization
2431
2432 For more details on this argument, see the ODEFunction documentation.
2433
2434 ## Fields
2435
2436 The fields of the DynamicalBVPFunction type directly match the names of the inputs.
2437 """
2438 struct DynamicalBVPFunction{
2439 iip, specialize, twopoint, F, BF, TMM, Ta, Tt, TJ, BCTJ, JVP, VJP,
2440 JP, BCJP, BCRP, SP, TW, TWt, TPJ, O, TCV, BCTCV,
2441 SYS, ID} <: AbstractBVPFunction{iip, twopoint}

2465 @doc doc"""
2466 IntegralFunction{iip,specialize,F,T} <: AbstractIntegralFunction{iip}
2467
2468 A representation of an integrand `f` defined by:
2469
2470 ```math
2471 f(u, p)
2472 ```
2473
2474 For an in-place form of `f` see the `iip` section below for details on in-place or
2475 out-of-place handling.
2476
2477 ```julia
2478 IntegralFunction{iip,specialize}(f, [integrand_prototype])
2479 ```
2480
2481 Note that only `f` is required, and in the case of inplace integrands a mutable array
2482 `integrand_prototype` to store the result of the integrand. If `integrand_prototype` is
2483 present for either in-place or out-of-place integrands it is used to infer the return type
2484 of the integrand.
2485
2486 ## iip: In-Place vs Out-Of-Place
2487
2488 Out-of-place functions must be of the form ``y = f(u, p)`` and in-place functions of the form
2489 ``f(y, u, p)``, where `y` is a number or array containing the output. Since `f` is allowed to return any type (e.g. real or complex numbers or
2490 arrays), in-place functions must provide a container `integrand_prototype` that is of the
2491 right type and size for the variable ``y``, and the result is written to this container in-place.
2492 When in-place forms are used, in-place array operations, i.e. broadcasting, may be used by
2493 algorithms to reduce allocations. If `integrand_prototype` is not provided, `f` is assumed
2494 to be out-of-place.
2495
2496 ## specialize
2497
2498 This field is currently unused
2499
2500 ## Fields
2501
2502 The fields of the IntegralFunction type directly match the names of the inputs.
2503 """
2504 struct IntegralFunction{iip, specialize, F, T} <:
2505 AbstractIntegralFunction{iip}
2506 f::F
2507 integrand_prototype::T
2508 end
2509
2510 @doc doc"""
2511 BatchIntegralFunction{iip,specialize,F,T} <: AbstractIntegralFunction{iip}
2512
2513 A batched representation of an (non-batched) integrand `f(u, p)` that can be
2514 evaluated at multiple points simultaneously using threads, the gpu, or
2515 distributed memory defined by:
2516
2517 ```math
2518 by = bf(bu, p)
2519 ```
2520
2521 Here we prefix variables with `b` to indicate they are batched variables, which
2522 implies that they are arrays whose **last** dimension is reserved for batching
2523 different evaluation points, or function values, and may be of a variable
2524 length. ``bu`` is an array whose elements correspond to distinct evaluation
2525 points to `f`, and `bf` is a function to evaluate `f` 'point-wise' so that
2526 `f(bu[..., i], p) == bf(bu, p)[..., i]`. For example, a simple batching implementation
2527 of a scalar, univariate function is via broadcasting: `bf(bu, p) = f.(bu, Ref(p))`,
2528 although this interface exists in order to allow user parallelization.
2529 In general, the integration algorithm is allowed to vary the number of
2530 evaluation points between subsequent calls to `bf`.
2531
2532 For an in-place form of `bf` see the `iip` section below for details on in-place
2533 or out-of-place handling.
2534
2535 ```julia
2536 BatchIntegralFunction{iip,specialize}(bf, [integrand_prototype];
2537 max_batch=typemax(Int))
2538 ```
2539 Note that only `bf` is required, and in the case of inplace integrands a mutable
2540 array `integrand_prototype` to store a batch of integrand evaluations, with
2541 a last "batching" dimension.
2542
2543 The keyword `max_batch` is used to set a soft limit on the number of points to
2544 batch at the same time so that memory usage is controlled.
2545
2546 If `integrand_prototype` is present for either in-place or out-of-place integrands it is
2547 used to infer the return type of the integrand.
2548
2549 ## iip: In-Place vs Out-Of-Place
2550
2551 Out-of-place functions must be of the form `by = bf(bu, p)` and in-place
2552 functions of the form `bf(by, bu, p)` where `by` is a batch array containing the
2553 output. Since the algorithm may vary the number of points to batch, the batching
2554 dimension can be of any length, including zero, and since `bf` is allowed to
2555 return arrays of any type (e.g. real or complex) or size, in-place functions
2556 must provide a container `integrand_prototype` of the desired type and size for
2557 `by`. If `integrand_prototype` is not provided, `bf` is assumed to be
2558 out-of-place.
2559
2560 In the out-of-place case, we require `f(bu[..., i], p) == bf(bu, p)[..., i]`,
2561 and certain algorithms, such as those implemented in C, may infer the type or
2562 shape of `by` by calling `bf` with an empty array of input points, i.e. `bu`
2563 with `size(bu)[end] == 0`. Then it is expected for the resulting `by` to have
2564 the same type and `size(by)[begin:end-1]` for all subsequent calls.
2565
2566 When the in-place form is used, we require `f(by[..., i], bu[..., i], p) ==
2567 bf(by, bu, p)[..., i]` and `size(by)[begin:end-1] ==
2568 size(integrand_prototype)[begin:end-1]`. The algorithm should always pass the
2569 integrand `by` arrays that are `similar` to `integrand_prototype`, and may use
2570 views and in-place array operations to reduce allocations.
2571
2572 ## specialize
2573
2574 This field is currently unused
2575
2576 ## Fields
2577
2578 The fields of the BatchIntegralFunction type are `f`, corresponding to `bf`
2579 above, and `integrand_prototype`.
2580 """
2581 struct BatchIntegralFunction{iip, specialize, F, T} <:
2582 AbstractIntegralFunction{iip}
2583 f::F
2584 integrand_prototype::T
2585 max_batch::Int
2586 end

4775 function ODEInputFunction{iip, specialize}(f;
4776 mass_matrix = __has_mass_matrix(f) ? f.mass_matrix :
4777 I,
4778 analytic = __has_analytic(f) ? f.analytic : nothing,
4779 tgrad = __has_tgrad(f) ? f.tgrad : nothing,
4780 jac = __has_jac(f) ? f.jac : nothing,
4781 controljac = __has_controljac(f) ? f.controljac : nothing,
4782 jvp = __has_jvp(f) ? f.jvp : nothing,
4783 vjp = __has_vjp(f) ? f.vjp : nothing,
4784 jac_prototype = __has_jac_prototype(f) ?
4785 f.jac_prototype :
4786 nothing,
4787 controljac_prototype = __has_controljac_prototype(f) ?
4788 f.controljac_prototype :
4789 nothing,
4790 sparsity = __has_sparsity(f) ? f.sparsity :
4791 jac_prototype,
4792 Wfact = __has_Wfact(f) ? f.Wfact : nothing,
4793 Wfact_t = __has_Wfact_t(f) ? f.Wfact_t : nothing,
4794 W_prototype = __has_W_prototype(f) ? f.W_prototype : nothing,
4795 paramjac = __has_paramjac(f) ? f.paramjac : nothing,
4796 syms = nothing,
4797 indepsym = nothing,
4798 paramsyms = nothing,
4799 observed = __has_observed(f) ? f.observed :
4800 DEFAULT_OBSERVED,
4801 colorvec = __has_colorvec(f) ? f.colorvec : nothing,
4802 sys = __has_sys(f) ? f.sys : nothing,
4803 initializeprob = __has_initializeprob(f) ? f.initializeprob : nothing,
4804 update_initializeprob! = __has_update_initializeprob!(f) ?
4805 f.update_initializeprob! : nothing,
4806 initializeprobmap = __has_initializeprobmap(f) ? f.initializeprobmap : nothing,
4807 initializeprobpmap = __has_initializeprobpmap(f) ? f.initializeprobpmap : nothing,
4808 initialization_data = __has_initialization_data(f) ? f.initialization_data :
4809 nothing,
4810 nlstep_data = __has_nlstep_data(f) ? f.nlstep_data : nothing
4811 ) where {iip,
4812 specialize
4813 }
4814 if mass_matrix === I && f isa Tuple
4815 mass_matrix = ((I for i in 1:length(f))...,)
4816 end
4817
4818 if (specialize === FunctionWrapperSpecialize) &&
4819 !(f isa FunctionWrappersWrappers.FunctionWrappersWrapper)
4820 error("FunctionWrapperSpecialize must be used on the problem constructor for access to u0, p, and t types!")
4821 end
4822
4823 if jac === nothing && isa(jac_prototype, AbstractSciMLOperator)
4824 if iip
4825 jac = (J, x, u, p, t) -> update_coefficients!(J, x, p, t) #(J,x,u,p,t)
4826 else
4827 jac = (x, u, p, t) -> update_coefficients(deepcopy(jac_prototype), x, p, t)
4828 end
4829 end
4830
4831 if controljac === nothing && isa(controljac_prototype, AbstractSciMLOperator)
4832 if iip_bc
4833 controljac = (J, x, u, p, t) -> update_coefficients!(J, u, p, t) #(J,x,u,p,t)
4834 else
4835 controljac = (
4836 x, u, p, t) -> update_coefficients(deepcopy(controljac_prototype), u, p, t)
4837 end
4838 end
4839
4840 if jac_prototype !== nothing && colorvec === nothing &&
4841 ArrayInterface.fast_matrix_colors(jac_prototype)
4842 _colorvec = ArrayInterface.matrix_colors(jac_prototype)
4843 else
4844 _colorvec = colorvec
4845 end
4846
4847 jaciip = jac !== nothing ? isinplace(jac, 5, "jac", iip) : iip
4848 controljaciip = controljac !== nothing ? isinplace(controljac, 5, "controljac", iip) :
4849 iip
4850 tgradiip = tgrad !== nothing ? isinplace(tgrad, 5, "tgrad", iip) : iip
4851 jvpiip = jvp !== nothing ? isinplace(jvp, 6, "jvp", iip) : iip
4852 vjpiip = vjp !== nothing ? isinplace(vjp, 6, "vjp", iip) : iip
4853 Wfactiip = Wfact !== nothing ? isinplace(Wfact, 6, "Wfact", iip) : iip
4854 Wfact_tiip = Wfact_t !== nothing ? isinplace(Wfact_t, 6, "Wfact_t", iip) : iip
4855 paramjaciip = paramjac !== nothing ? isinplace(paramjac, 5, "paramjac", iip) : iip
4856
4857 nonconforming = (jaciip, tgradiip, jvpiip, vjpiip, Wfactiip, Wfact_tiip,
4858 paramjaciip) .!= iip
4859 if any(nonconforming)
4860 nonconforming = findall(nonconforming)
4861 functions = ["jac", "tgrad", "jvp", "vjp", "Wfact", "Wfact_t", "paramjac"][nonconforming]
4862 throw(NonconformingFunctionsError(functions))
4863 end

4865 _f = prepare_function(f)
4866
4867 sys = sys_or_symbolcache(sys, syms, paramsyms, indepsym)
4868 initdata = reconstruct_initialization_data(
4869 initialization_data, initializeprob, update_initializeprob!,
4870 initializeprobmap, initializeprobpmap)
4871
4872 if specialize === NoSpecialize
4873 ODEInputFunction{iip, specialize,
4874 Any, Any, Any, Any,
4875 Any, Any, Any, Any, typeof(jac_prototype), typeof(controljac_prototype),
4876 typeof(sparsity), Any, Any, typeof(W_prototype), Any,
4877 Any,
4878 typeof(_colorvec),
4879 typeof(sys), Union{Nothing, OverrideInitData}}(
4880 _f, mass_matrix, analytic, tgrad, jac, controljac,
4881 jvp, vjp, jac_prototype, controljac_prototype, sparsity, Wfact,
4882 Wfact_t, W_prototype, paramjac,
4883 observed, _colorvec, sys, initdata)
4884 elseif specialize === false
4885 ODEInputFunction{iip, FunctionWrapperSpecialize,
4886 typeof(_f), typeof(mass_matrix), typeof(analytic), typeof(tgrad),
4887 typeof(jac), typeof(controljac), typeof(jvp), typeof(vjp),
4888 typeof(jac_prototype), typeof(controljac_prototype),
4889 typeof(sparsity), typeof(Wfact), typeof(Wfact_t), typeof(W_prototype),
4890 typeof(paramjac),
4891 typeof(observed),
4892 typeof(_colorvec),
4893 typeof(sys), typeof(initdata)}(_f, mass_matrix,
4894 analytic, tgrad, jac, controljac,
4895 jvp, vjp, jac_prototype, controljac_prototype, sparsity, Wfact,
4896 Wfact_t, W_prototype, paramjac,
4897 observed, _colorvec, sys, initdata)
4898 else
4899 ODEInputFunction{iip, specialize,
4900 typeof(_f), typeof(mass_matrix), typeof(analytic), typeof(tgrad),
4901 typeof(jac), typeof(controljac), typeof(jvp), typeof(vjp),
4902 typeof(jac_prototype), typeof(controljac_prototype),
4903 typeof(sparsity), typeof(Wfact), typeof(Wfact_t), typeof(W_prototype),
4904 typeof(paramjac),
4905 typeof(observed),
4906 typeof(_colorvec),
4907 typeof(sys), typeof(initdata)}(
4908 _f, mass_matrix, analytic, tgrad,
4909 jac, controljac, jvp, vjp, jac_prototype, controljac_prototype, sparsity, Wfact,
4910 Wfact_t, W_prototype, paramjac,
4911 observed, _colorvec, sys, initdata)
4912 end
4913 end

4926 function sys_or_symbolcache(sys, syms, paramsyms, indepsym = nothing)
4927 if sys === nothing &&
4928 (syms !== nothing || paramsyms !== nothing || indepsym !== nothing)
4929 Base.depwarn(
4930 "The use of keyword arguments `syms`, `paramsyms` and `indepsym` for `SciMLFunction`s is deprecated. Pass `sys = SymbolCache(syms, paramsyms, indepsym)` instead.",
4931 :syms)
4932 sys = SymbolCache(syms, paramsyms, indepsym)
4933 end
4934 return sys
4935 end
4936
4937 function reconstruct_initialization_data(
4938 initdata, initprob, update_initprob!, initprobmap, initprobpmap)
4939 if initdata === nothing && initprob !== nothing
4940 initdata = OverrideInitData(initprob, update_initprob!, initprobmap, initprobpmap)
4941 end
4942 return initdata
4943 end

5193 function SymbolicIndexingInterface.observed(fn::AbstractSciMLFunction, sym)
5194 if has_observed(fn) && fn.observed !== DEFAULT_OBSERVED &&
5195 fn.observed !== DEFAULT_OBSERVED_NO_TIME
5196 if hasmethod(fn.observed, Tuple{Any})
5197 return fn.observed(sym)
5198 else
5199 return (args...) -> fn.observed(sym, args...)
5200 end
5201 end
5202 if has_sys(fn) &&
5203 hasmethod(SymbolicIndexingInterface.observed, Tuple{typeof(fn.sys), typeof(sym)})
5204 return SymbolicIndexingInterface.observed(fn.sys, sym)
5205 end
5206 error("SciMLFunction does not have observed")
5207 end

5210 return SymbolicIndexingInterface.observed(fn, getproperty(fn.sys, sym))

5226 function Base.getproperty(x::HomotopyNonlinearFunction, sym::Symbol)
5227 if hasfield(HomotopyNonlinearFunction, sym)
5228 return getfield(x, sym)
5229 elseif hasfield(NonlinearFunction, sym)
5230 return getfield(getfield(x, :f), sym)
5231 elseif (sym == :initializeprob || sym == :update_initializeprob! ||
5232 sym == :initializeprobmap || sym == :initializeprobpmap)
5233 f = getfield(x, :f)
5234 if f.initialization_data === nothing
5235 return nothing
5236 else
5237 return getproperty(f.initialization_data, sym)
5238 end
5239 end
5240 end
5241
5242 function Base.getproperty(x::AbstractSciMLFunction, sym::Symbol)
5243 if __has_initialization_data(x) &&
5244 (sym == :initializeprob || sym == :update_initializeprob! ||
5245 sym == :initializeprobmap || sym == :initializeprobpmap)
5246 if x.initialization_data === nothing
5247 return nothing
5248 else
5249 return getproperty(x.initialization_data, sym)
5250 end
5251 end
5252 return getfield(x, sym)
5253 end
